newsitem.title: USA: Georgia sees 2.8 percent job growth in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Georgia sees 2.8 percent job growth in 1996.

text.p: Georgia added 98,200 new jobs in 1996, an increase of 2.8 percent over last year, state Labor Commissioner David Poythress said.

"These new figures on job growth, combined with our continuing low unemployment rate, which has averaged 4.5 percent for the year, and other year-end economic indicators, show that Georgia's economy continues to do much better than the nation as a whole," Poythress said. "We expect our economy and our jobs to continue to grow at a moderate pace in 1997.
Georgia employment rose to 3.61 million in 1996 from 3.52 million in 1995, with 72,300 of the new jobs in trade and services.
Strong gains were seen in temporary employment agencies, security firms, health care facilities, amusements, computer and data processing, engineering, accounting, research and management firms.
Building supply retailers and restaurants created 29,900 jobs while manufacturing of durable goods added 7,500.
Employment totals, new jobs, and job growth rates for Georgia's major cities in 1996 were:
Albany, 61,100 jobs, an increase of 1,000 jobs or 1.7 percent.
Athens, 74,800 jobs, an increase of 3,200 jobs or 4.5 percent.
Atlanta, 1.95 million jobs, an increase of 69,900 jobs or 3.7 percent.
Augusta, 194,300 jobs, an increase of 2,000 jobs or 1 perent.
Columbus, 115,400 jobs, an increase of 3,500 jobs or 3.1 percent.
Macon, 146,300 jobs, an increase of 2,300 jobs or 1.6 percent.
Savannah, 134,300 jobs, an increase of 4,300 jobs or 3,3 percent.
